question: What is the sum of the deviations of the values of the data set 5, 6, 7,9, 10, 12 and 14, from the mean of the values given in the same date set?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the fundamental property of **Arithmetic Mean**, the sum of the **deviations** of all observations from their **mean** is always **zero**.

∑(xᵢ − x̄) = 0

Therefore, without any calculation, the sum is 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1a6acc29d521bdebc151f938c1a0385e687719e981233688762275e75e91f7f7.png] 

**Given:** Data set = 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 14

**Formula Used:** Mean (x̄) = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations

⇒ Sum = 5 + 6 + 7 + 9 + 10 + 12 + 14 = 63

⇒ Number of terms (n) = 7

⇒ Mean (x̄) = 63 ÷ 7 = 9

⇒ Deviations from Mean: (5−9), (6−9), (7−9), (9−9), (10−9), (12−9), (14−9)

⇒ Deviations = −4, −3, −2, 0, 1, 3, 5

⇒ Sum of Deviations = (−4) + (−3) + (−2) + 0 + 1 + 3 + 5

⇒ Sum of Deviations = −9 + 9 = 0

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Property of Arithmetic Mean

The algebraic sum of **deviations** of a set of observations from their **arithmetic mean** is always **zero**.

Sum of Squared Deviations

The sum of the **squares of deviations** of the items from their arithmetic mean is **minimum** compared to any other value.

Mean of Discrete Series

For a **discrete series**, the mean is calculated as x̄ = (∑fᵢxᵢ) ÷ ∑fᵢ.</p
